subject: Spike of 5xx/429 from Dedicated - connection resets seen
messages:
From: Sanjay Kapoor <sanjay.kapoor@fastpay.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <cto@fastpay.com>
Date: 2026-10-07T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden surge of 5xx/429 — Dedicated (fastpay-prod)

Hi Laura,

We're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx/429 responses from Redwood for our production traffic (fastpay-prod) starting ~08:00 PDT. Latency jumps to 4-6s for many requests, and our client logs show TLS connection resets followed by repeated retries. Sample rows attached (fastpay_error_log.csv).

What we know:
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated (us-west-2) - dedicated pool id rdw-ded-78f
- Symptoms: repeated 503/502 and 429s, connection reset (RST) TCP flags observed, and lots of SYN retransmits from our outbound NAT IPs.
- Impact: user-facing payments failing (~12% of transactions) and retries are amplifying load.

We need immediate help — can you confirm whether anything changed on Redwood's side (routing, firewall rules, peering config) and if you can look at per-request logs or health of the dedicated pool? We can run tcpdump/flow logs if useful (I've attached a short CSV and can provide pcaps).

Please escalate — our CTO (Alicia) is on copy.

Thanks,
Sanjay Kapoor
Head of Payments Ops, FastPay

Subject: Re: Sudden surge of 5xx/429 — Dedicated (fastpay-prod)

Sanjay — thanks for the quick heads up and the CSV. We're treating this as high priority. Initial ack: we've reproduced the error signatures in our logs (increased 5xx + backend connection resets against rdw-ded-78f).

Immediate asks:
- Please send a small tcpdump (10s) capturing SYN/RST around 08:00 PDT and the example request IDs if possible (I see request ids in your CSV).
- If you can pull VPC flow logs (ENI-level) for the time window, that would help correlate SYN retransmits vs. application-level failures.

Actions I'm taking:
- Looping in engineering (Rishi) to investigate NAT/conn-tracking and firewall state.
- Marcus will open an SLA incident and track communications.
- We'll propose mitigations (backoff on your side to reduce retry amplification + temporary failover to an alternate Redwood endpoint).

I'll arrange a quick bridge in 15 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we're on it.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-07T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden surge of 5xx/429 — Dedicated (fastpay-prod)

Quick triage notes (from initial log sweep):
- We see a pattern of TCP connection resets (RST) and unusually high SYN retransmits from FastPay egress IPs to our dedicated pool. The Redis/KV backend and model workers are healthy.
- Suspected causes in order:
  1) NAT port exhaustion on FastPay side (ephemeral port reuse leading to connection resets)
  2) Firewall / stateful connection-tracking limits dropping established connections (conntrack table full)
  3) Intermittent DNS anomalies causing rapid failover and duplicate concurrent connections

Immediate mitigation suggestions for FastPay (to reduce customer impact):
- Reduce client retry frequency and increase retry backoff (avoid tight 100ms retries).
- Temporarily direct a fraction of traffic to our alternate Dedicated endpoint in us-east-1 (we can accept a weight-based split).

What we need from FastPay:
- tcpdump pcap focused on 443 to rdw-ded-78f at 08:00–08:10 (attach as fastpay_tcpdump_1007.pcap).
- VPC flow logs and NAT gateway metrics (SNAT port utilization).

I've created JIRA SUP-4521 to track the root-cause. Marcus, please add this to the SLA incident.

I'll also open a ticket with AWS if we see NAT gateway saturation.

—Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments referenced: none (awaiting FastPay pcap)

Date: 2026-10-07T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden surge of 5xx/429 — Dedicated (fastpay-prod)

Update from our analysis of the flow logs you provided (thanks Sanjay). Attached a short pcap extract and a flow summary image (flow_summary.png). Observations:
- Multiple SYN retransmit bursts from FastPay egress IPs toward our ELB/ENIs in us-west-2 starting 08:00:40.
- ENI-level metrics show many connections entering CLOSE_WAIT quickly; remote side is sending RSTs.
- No obvious increase in upstream latency or CPU on Redwood workers.

Probable immediate cause: stateful firewall/NAT on FastPay side hitting connection tracking or port exhaustion — the pattern fits conntrack/NAT contention rather than an application bug on our fleet.

Temporary remediation options:
1) FastPay: increase conntrack table and ephemeral ports, or add another NAT gateway to increase SNAT port pool.
2) Redwood: perform a canary shift of 10-20% of FastPay traffic to our us-east-1 dedicated pool (rdw-ded-33b) to relieve the black hole; this requires FastPay changing egress route or us accepting TLS SNI fallback.

Can we get a quick call now (30 min) to agree on the short-term shift? I'll share the pcap snippet on the bridge.

Best,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-07T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Executive update: ongoing 5xx surge and remediation plan (FastPay)

Alicia — brief executive summary and action plan following today's incident affecting FastPay (we are on conference with ops now):

Summary:
- Incident: increased 5xx/429 + connection resets for FastPay's Dedicated pool (rdw-ded-78f) starting ~08:00 PDT. Peak impact lasted ~90 minutes and currently trending down after mitigation steps.
- Root cause (preliminary): network-side connection tracking / NAT port exhaustion on FastPay egress leading to TCP resets and request duplication/retries. Redwood fleet and model workers are healthy.

Remediation and timeline:
- Short term (now): FastPay to increase NAT / conntrack capacity (recommended immediate change). Redwood performed a partial traffic shift to us-east-1 (rdw-ded-33b) for 20% of traffic — this reduced error amplification.
- Mid term (24–72 hrs): joint runbook execution to harden retry/backoff patterns, add health-check routing and an automated fallback to alternate dedicated pool.
- Next steps: joint RCA (detailed) to be delivered by 10/10. We're capturing pcap + flow logs and Jira is SUP-4521.

Compensation: we'll propose a targeted service credit for the impacted window; Marcus will follow up with formal SLA remediation and next steps.

We're committed to full transparency and will provide the RCA and mitigation checklist. If you'd like a single-threaded exec owner, Vanessa Ortiz (cc'd) will lead the Redwood exec interface.

Apologies again for the disruption — please let us know any questions.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
